title: Show the consultation step before the service starts
simple_explanation: A short consultation before the service helps the customer feel heard. It shows your stylist listens and plans before starting.
do_this: Before any haircut or colour, ask the customer three questions: what length, what look, and any past hair problem.
Write the answers in a small notepad near the chair.
Show two similar work photos from your phone if you have permission to use them.
Ask one final question: 'Shall I start with this plan?'
Keep the same question list at every chair so staff follow the same process.
copy_ready_text: Before we start, can I ask 3 quick questions? What length do you want? Any hair issue? Do you have a photo of the look you like? I will plan the steps first. - {{businessName}}
example_for_business: At {{businessName}} in {{location}}, the stylist keeps a small notepad by the chair and writes the customer's length, look, and past hair issue before starting the service.
why_this_works: Most bad-result fear comes from being misunderstood. A two-minute consultation shows the customer that the stylist has listened before touching the hair.
how_to_know_it_worked: Track how many haircut or colour customers finish without asking for changes. Also note how many complaints mention 'not what I asked for'.

title: Send a polite WhatsApp message when the slot is late
simple_explanation: When your chair or stylist is running late, a quick honest WhatsApp message keeps trust. Hiding the delay makes customers more upset.
do_this: Send the message as soon as you know the delay.
Keep it short: sorry, reason, new time, and a choice.
Offer two options: wait for the next chair or shift to a later slot.
Save this as a WhatsApp Business quick reply.
If the delay becomes longer, send one more short update.
copy_ready_text: Hi, sorry. Your slot at {{businessName}} is running about {{delayMinutes}} minutes late. You can wait, or I can shift you to {{newTime}}. Which is better for you?
example_for_business: At {{businessName}} in {{location}}, when a colour service takes longer than planned, the front desk sends this saved WhatsApp reply and lets the customer choose whether to wait or shift.
why_this_works: Customers can accept a delay when they know what is happening. A clear update with two choices feels respectful and reduces angry waiting.
how_to_know_it_worked: Count how many late-slot customers still arrive after receiving the message. Also track complaints about waiting time each week.

title: Send simple aftercare steps after the service
simple_explanation: Customers forget what to do at home after a facial, colour, or styling service. A short written note reduces confusion.
do_this: Pick the three services that need aftercare, like hair colour, facial, or styling.
Write three simple aftercare points for each service.
Give the customer the card before payment.
Send the same points on WhatsApp the same evening.
Add one line telling them to message the salon if they feel itching, redness, or hair trouble.
copy_ready_text: After your {{serviceName}} today: 1) Follow the wash timing we told you. 2) Avoid heat, sweat, or harsh products today. 3) Message {{businessName}} if you feel itching, redness, or hair trouble.
example_for_business: At {{businessName}} in {{location}}, the stylist gives a small aftercare card after hair colour and sends the same points on WhatsApp in the evening.
why_this_works: Written aftercare is easier to remember than verbal advice. It also shows the customer that the salon cares after the bill is paid.
how_to_know_it_worked: Check whether fewer customers call asking what to do after the service. Track aftercare questions and skin or hair complaints each week.
